obtained.how: Environment Canada's digitized copy of the paper's typescript, same title and author ('Advances in defining critical loading levels for phosphorus in lake eutrophication / by Richard A. Vollenweider', Government of Canada Publications catalogue En37-475/1979E-PDF, 'digitized edition from print'); undated, references to 1975, footnote 'part of the OECD Cooperative Programme on Eutrophication'; typescript pages 1-29 plus references, tables, appendices and figures. Retrieved from the Wayback Machine's 2021-11-08 capture of the publications.gc.ca PDF (the live address now opens an 'archived content' notice that needs a browser cookie). This is NOT the typeset Memorie article: its pagination and equation numbers may differ from the published pp. 53-83

claims.claim: 1/(1+√τ) (τ the water residence time, years) is Vollenweider's ratio of lake to inflow phosphorus concentration
claims.location: typescript p. 21 (PDF p. 22), eq. 14; defined at typescript p. 10 (PDF p. 11), eq. 6; derived at typescript p. 14 (PDF p. 15), eq. 10
claims.conditions: eq. 6 defines πr = τp/τw (residence time of P relative to that of water) as 'the ratio between average lake concentration, [P]λ, and the average inflow concentration [P]j'; eq. 10 approximates τp/τw = 1/(1+√τw) = 1/(1+√(z̄/qs)), chosen so that τp/τw → 1 as τw → 0; eq. 14 states the expected statistical relation πr = [P]λ/[P]j ≈ 1/(1+√τw); eq. 13 (typescript p. 17) gives lake P = (Lp/qs)·1/(1+√(z̄/qs)), Lp/qs being the average inflow concentration. τw is the filling time V/Qy in years; qs = z̄/τw the hydraulic load (m/y)
claims.note: equation numbers and pages are the typescript's; the Memorie article's numbering was not seen

claims.claim: the Larsen–Mercier retention is R = 1/(1+√ρ) with ρ = 1/τ the flushing rate, so 1/(1+√τ) is its complement, the share of the load that leaves
claims.quote: This, indeed, is identical to what one would derive from Eq. (6)
claims.conditions: Vollenweider quotes Larsen & Mercier (1975, EPA working paper) for Rc = 1/(1+√ρw) and shows it follows from his ratio: Rc = ([P]j·Q − [P]λ·Q)/([P]j·Q) = 1 − πr (eq. 15), hence Rc = √τw/(1+√τw) = √(z̄/qs)/(1+√(z̄/qs)) = 1/(1+√ρw) (eq. 16), or √z̄/(√qs+√z̄) (eq. 16a)
claims.note: at steady state the outflow concentration is the lake's, so 1 − Rc = [P]λ/[P]j = 1/(1+√τw) is the fraction of the inflowing P that leaves: the paper's reading is right

claims.paper: §5.2 ('the lakes kept 0.66–0.72 of their P load'; Larsen–Mercier 0.34 / 0.28 for water residence 0.27 and 0.15 years)
claims.claim: for τ = 0.27 and 0.15 yr, 1/(1+√τ) = 0.66 and 0.72 (the old calibration's 'retention') while R = √τ/(1+√τ) = 0.34 and 0.28
claims.location: typescript p. 14 (PDF p. 15), eq. 10; p. 26 (PDF p. 27), eq. 16
claims.conditions: project arithmetic on the source's formulas

notes: Caveats for the rewrite. (1) Eq. 10 was fitted to 21 lakes with τw ≥ 1 yr: 'Lakes having τw < 1 have been excluded' (typescript p. 11, Fig. 3), and Vollenweider warns the dependency 'cannot be linearly extrapolated below τw < 1' (p. 14); Hot Brook's τ of 0.15-0.27 yr lies outside the fitted range (eq. 10 was built to tend to 1 as τw → 0). (2) He notes the statistical fit gives 0.6-0.7 at τw = 1 against the formula's 0.5, so eq. 10 may slightly underestimate τp/τw below τw = 1 (p. 14), and that Rc may be slightly underestimated for qs < 10 m/y (p. 27); Hot Brook's qs ≈ z̄/τ ≈ 3.0/0.27 ≈ 11 and 2.55/0.15 ≈ 17 m/y (project arithmetic), where he finds 'fair agreement' with Kirchner & Dillon. Other values: critical spring-overturn total P 10 mg/m3 (lower limit, oligotrophic) to 20 (upper, eutrophic side); apparent settling velocity ≈ 10 m/y (typescript p. 6); Lc = 10·qs·(1+√(z̄/qs)) mg P m-2 y-1 (eq. 11a, p. 14); chlorophyll against (Lp/qs)/(1+√τw) for ~60 lakes, r = 0.868 (p. 18); periphyton (Cladophora) problems expected above average inflow concentrations of 30-40 mg P/m3 (p. 23). Vollenweider's Larsen & Mercier source is the 1975 EPA working paper (No. 174); the paper's references list the 1976 J. Fish. Res. Board Can. article.
